recognize_zh: 組織中一顆大型顆粒，中心呈淡嗜伊紅、可見細小裂隙與纖維狀結構，邊緣有一圈深紫色放射狀絲狀菌帶，周圍被嗜中性球與出血包圍；這種「硫磺顆粒」（sulfur granule）是放線菌病（Actinomyces）的典型表現。
features: Large, well-demarcated granule (colony) with a pale eosinophilic, finely fibrillary center containing needle-like clefts
Dense basophilic band of radiating filaments at the peripheral edge (upper margin)
Eosinophilic club-like fringe (Splendore-Hoeppli material) at portions of the periphery
Surrounding rim of neutrophils admixed with red cells and golden-brown hemosiderin/fibrin
Loose fibrous stroma in the background
describe_en: H&E-stained section of a peritoneal nodule shows a large, well-circumscribed granule within a neutrophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate with hemorrhage and hemosiderin deposition. The granule has a pale eosinophilic, fibrillary center and a basophilic peripheral band of radiating filaments with an eosinophilic club-like fringe. The surrounding tissue shows loose fibrous stroma. Findings are consistent with a sulfur granule of actinomycosis; Gram and GMS stains highlighting branching gram-positive filaments and culture are recommended for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Nocardia rarely forms true granules, and its beaded branching filaments are modified acid-fast positive, whereas Actinomyces is acid-fast negative.
Botryomycotic granules are composed of gram-positive cocci or gram-negative bacilli rather than thin branching filaments.
Fungal grains contain broad septate hyphae (3-5 um) with chlamydospores on GMS/PAS, much thicker than bacterial filaments (<1 um).

ddx.dx: Hyphal fungal ball (e.g., Aspergillus) or calcified debris
ddx.vs: Aspergillus shows acute-angle branching septate hyphae without a Splendore-Hoeppli fringe, and calcific debris lacks filaments on Gram stain.
